description: The same 3D-topology frame (field topopt3d-petg-mid-133-d385cf32ab, drawn at DRAWING_VERSION 17, surface_open_mm 0.3, fea_surface_mm 0.5) put through gates/structure.py's CalculiX checks in each filament the Snapmaker U1 can print: first mode held at the FC posts and saddle, drop and wall-hit floors with the drone as a free body. Every row converged (base 307559 tets vs fine 302050; mode within 5 %, crashes within 10 %), every solve in equilibrium (residual under 0.05 N).

extractions.what: On this frame only PA6-CF (drop 8.12 m, wall 3.66 m/s, 196 Hz, 13.8 g) and PAHT-CF (7.76 m, 3.44 m/s, 193 Hz, 13.4 g) clear both crash floors (1 m, 3 m/s); PA6-CF clears them by the most
extractions.note: CalculiX floors: first point to reach the printed strength, no plastic work, no floor give; P1 settles the real number.

extractions.what: Of the filaments that need nothing extra on the U1, PETG survives the most: drop 2.04 m (clears 1 m), wall 1.67 m/s (misses 3 m/s), at 16.2 g and 143 Hz. PLA is weaker (1.57 m, 1.46 m/s); ASA (1.97 m, 176 Hz) needs the top cover; PETG-CF (1.62 m) a hardened nozzle; TPU95A guard arcs lower the mode (136 Hz) and gain nothing in a crash (1.94 m, 1.61 m/s)

note: Written by the scratchpad's compare_multi.py + collect.py on 2026-10-18; crash rows use each filament as its own strong material.
